title: Camp 4 close: the whole Japji
hook: thirty-eight pauris and two saloks, from sochai soch to the faces that shine

segments.voice: Yesterday, pavan, in the final salok: air, water, earth. Today, the last day of this camp, and a look back at the whole Japji.

Seventy-four days ago, this camp began with an alphabet. Thirty-five letters, the Guru's alphabet, and a promise: you'd hear each stanza before trying to understand it. Then the Mool Mantar, sounded out. Then one word, jap, recite, remember. Then, one pauri at a time, the whole thing. Some people have recited the Japji every morning since childhood; some have never heard a line of it. This path has put you somewhere in between: you've walked it, stanza by stanza, from the first line to the last. That's worth stopping for.
screen: `SEVENTY-FOUR DAYS AGO: AN ALPHABET.` → `ONE PAURI AT A TIME.` → `THE WHOLE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Here is the Japji, all of it, in one breath. The Mool Mantar, Ik Onkar, one Creator, and a salok: aad sach, true in the beginning, true now. Pauri 1: sochai soch, thinking a hundred thousand times won't get you there; walk in the hukam, the order. The order holding everything, and haumai, the I, I, that forgets it. The Giver who never tires. The early hours and nadar, the kindly glance. Four stanzas of suniai, listening, and four of mannai, trusting. Asankh, the countless: devotions, fools, names. The ant who remembers. Even hunger counted as a gift. Four stanzas for the yogis: contentment for earrings, wisdom for food, the One who sees though unseen, storehouses filled once, for all. Then the ladder: one tongue becoming millions, the steps to the Beloved, no power of our own. The five realms: Dharam Khand, this earth, a house for right action. Gian Khand, so many worlds. Saram Khand, the workshop where effort shapes the mind. Karam Khand, grace. Sach Khand, where the Formless dwells, hard as steel to tell. The goldsmith's shop where the Word is minted. And the closing salok: air the Guru, water the father, earth the mother, and faces that shine. Thirty-eight pauris and two saloks. Next, a new camp: the depths, stepping back from the Japji to see the whole Guru Granth Sahib: how it's built, whose voices are in it, and its great themes.
screen: `MOOL MANTAR AND AAD SACH.` · `LISTENING, TRUSTING, THE COUNTLESS.` · `THE YOGIS, THE LADDER.` · `FIVE REALMS, AND THE TRUE MINT.` · then, large: `I ACTUALLY READ IT.`

segments.voice: Let the stanzas come back on their own, in any order: the ant, the storehouses, the goldsmith's furnace, suniai, by listening. Whatever line surfaces, let it sit with you, say it quietly if you remember it, then let another come. If none comes, simply rest, breathing, in the quiet the Japji leaves behind.
Jap, recite, remember, the Japji's own title. The whole thing, thirty-eight pauris and two saloks, walked one stanza at a time, from sochai soch to the faces that shine.
Your line: I actually read it. From sochai soch to the faces that shine. Camp four, complete.

screen: `DAY 231 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: HOW THE GRANTH IS BUILT.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite the whole Japji Sahib every morning as the first bani of Nitnem, often from memory; it stands at the very start of the Guru Granth Sahib, on its first pages.
